repository_card.frontier: M0 Ising diagonalization is recorded; the forward/reverse finite transfer interfaces retain reconstruction and spectral inputs.
repository_card.bridge_hypothesis: Compare gaps only after naming their operators. Dictionary: normalized transfer eigenvalue ratio -> discrete correlation decay; channel subleading eigenvalue -> mixing rate. A Lindbladian can be nonnormal and the reverse correlation-to-gap implication needs observable visibility.
repository_card.next_finite_task: For a small transfer matrix and a small primitive channel, compute the full spectrum and an observable overlap table. Add a deliberately invisible slow mode as a negative control for the reverse interface.
repository_card.falsifier: Abandon a reverse-gap inference if the observable is orthogonal to the slow mode, or if a Liouvillian decay rate is substituted for a Hamiltonian energy gap.
repository_card.proposal_status: speculative; not executed or formally verified

sources.title: Depth-1 expanders on the unitary group and applications
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.source_claim: Anshu and collaborators construct constant-degree, constant-gap quantum expanders with depth-one local circuit realizations and apply them to one-dimensional Hamiltonians with an entanglement-gap relation.
sources.limits: An expander gap, a transfer gap and a many-body Hamiltonian gap are different operators. Track dimension, locality and the definition of gap before translating. First posted 1 September.

sources.title: Non-Abelian string melting and thermalization in an open lattice gauge theory
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.review_depth: v1: model, thermalization discussion and strong-dephasing reduction
sources.source_claim: A tensor-network study couples 1+1D SU(2) gauge theory with matter to a gauge-preserving Lindblad bath. It finds nonmonotonic relaxation and derives an exclusion-process description in a strong-dephasing limit.
sources.limits: This is an open-system finite/truncated lattice setting, not pure 4D Euclidean Yang-Mills. A Liouvillian relaxation rate is not automatically a Hamiltonian gap, and the strong-dephasing expansion has its own regime.
